question: Which insect spreads the malaria parasite to humans?
explanation: Spot on! Malaria is transmitted specifically when an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites looking for a blood meal.

question: Why do pregnant women and young children get severe malaria so easily in Nigeria?

options.A: Their immune defenses are either developing or temporarily lowered
options.B: They have a naturally higher body temperature that attracts vectors
options.C: They spend more time outdoors during peak sunlight hours
options.D: Their diets lack the specific nutrients required to fight protozoa

explanation: You got it! Little ones are still building their immune defenses, and pregnancy naturally lowers a woman's immune response for a bit, making them extra vulnerable.

question: What form of the malaria parasite does a mosquito first inject into a person?
explanation: Correct! Infected mosquitoes carry sporozoites in their salivary glands and inject them right into your skin and blood when they bite.

question: What happens inside red blood cells to cause those sudden, recurring fever spikes in malaria?

options.A: The rapid multiplication and bursting of red blood cells
options.B: The sudden drop in total white blood cell production
options.C: The allergic reaction to mosquito saliva in the skin
options.D: The physical blocking of large arteries in the heart

explanation: Well done! As the parasites multiply and burst out of red blood cells, they release toxins that trigger a sudden, intense fever.

question: Which sign tells you a patient has severe malaria instead of just uncomplicated malaria?
explanation: Spot on! Any sign of confusion, extreme weakness, or coma (cerebral malaria) means it's an emergency needing immediate inpatient care.

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fever and headache, but is fully alert and able to swallow drugs. How do you classify this?
explanation: Correct! Because the patient is stable and can take oral meds without danger signs, it's uncomplicated malaria. You'll see this a lot in clinical postings!

question: Why shouldn't nurses just give anti-malarials immediately to every patient with a fever without testing first?

options.A: RDT kits never work during the rainy season
options.B: Patients refuse to take medications without laboratory proof
options.C: Malaria drugs are too expensive to give out freely
options.D: Many other infections can cause similar symptoms to malaria

explanation: You got it! Illnesses like typhoid or UTIs can also cause fever. Testing first stops us from mistreating patients and wasting precious drugs.

question: What makes a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) so great for a busy rural health clinic?

options.A: It gives quick results from a finger-prick blood sample without complex equipment
options.B: It permanently prevents future mosquito bites from causing infection
options.C: It is the only test capable of identifying dead parasites after treatment
options.D: It tells the nurse the exact number of parasites circulating in the blood

explanation: Spot on! RDTs are fast, portable, and a lifesaver in clinics where there are no fancy lab machines or steady electricity.

question: Why do we combine two different drugs in Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy (ACT)?

options.A: To make the medication taste better for young children
options.B: To shorten the treatment duration to a single dose
options.C: To eliminate the need for any laboratory blood testing
options.D: To prevent or delay the development of parasite resistance

explanation: Correct! Teaming up two drugs with different actions helps wipe out all parasites cleanly and stops them from learning how to fight off the medicine.

question: A patient with severe malaria is admitted to your ward. How should they first receive their medication?
explanation: Well done! Severe cases move fast, so we need fast-acting injections (IV or IM artesunate) to get the drug into their system immediately.

question: What is the main goal of Intermittent Preventive Treatment in pregnancy (IPTp)?

options.A: To prevent the woman from ever being bitten by a mosquito
options.B: To boost the production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: To cure a severe case of cerebral malaria in the third trimester
options.D: To clear hidden parasites and protect the mother and baby

explanation: Spot on! IPTp is given during antenatal care to keep pregnant mums and their babies safe from the hidden dangers of malaria.

question: Why are Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) most effective when used while sleeping?

options.A: Anopheles mosquitoes bite mostly at night when people are asleep
options.B: It prevents mosquitoes from laying eggs inside household water pots
options.C: The chemical on the net repels daytime flies and cockroaches
options.D: It completely stops the flow of humid air into the bedroom

explanation: You got it! Since malaria mosquitoes love to hunt during the night, sleeping under a treated net hits them right when they are most active.

question: What causes severe anemia in a patient with advanced malaria?

options.A: A complete failure of dietary iron absorption in the gut
options.B: Sudden internal bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Suppression of kidney function leading to blood loss in urine
options.D: Destruction and rapid loss of red blood cells by the parasite

explanation: Correct! As the malaria parasites multiply and break open red blood cells en masse, the patient's blood count drops sharply, causing severe anemia.

question: An unconscious child with cerebral malaria is brought into the emergency ward. What is your very first nursing priority?

options.A: Ensuring a clear airway and monitoring breathing
options.B: Discharging the patient home with anti-malarial tablets
options.C: Encouraging the mother to feed the child oral porridge
options.D: Checking visual acuity using a Snellen eye chart

explanation: Spot on! ABCs come first in nursing. An unconscious child can easily choke or struggle to breathe, so keeping that airway open is priority number one.

question: How does health education in the community help reduce malaria cases?

options.A: It empowers families to use preventive tools and seek early testing
options.B: It replaces the need for hospital laboratories in rural zones
options.C: It provides immediate immunity to newborns in endemic regions
options.D: It permanently eliminates mosquito breeding sites nationwide

explanation: Well done! Teaching families how to use nets properly and report fevers early stops infections before they spiral out of control.

question: Which of these is NOT a standard community prevention message taught by nurses?

options.A: Attending antenatal clinics for preventive treatment during pregnancy
options.B: Sleeping inside insecticide-treated nets every single night
options.C: Taking high doses of antibiotics to prevent malaria infection
options.D: Clearing stagnant water puddles around residential houses

explanation: Correct! Antibiotics fight bacteria, not malaria parasites. Taking them for malaria is incorrect and only builds drug resistance.
